claims.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
claims.evidence: A shortest cycle remaining in G-S is induced and even. If its length were at least 10, eight consecutive vertices would induce P8, so it has length 4, 6, or 8. Conversely, an FVS meets every such cycle. When S is an FVS, each residual component is a P8-free tree, hence has diameter at most 6 and radius at most 3. Minimality implies that restoring any x creates a cycle through x; deleting x from that cycle leaves a path in one residual component between two neighbors of x.
claims.witness: The shortest-residual-cycle argument proves the equivalence; the cycle appearing in G-(S\{x}) certifies the final assertion.
claims.search_method: Direct reconstruction of all implications and boundary cases from the authorized files; no external search.

claims.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
claims.evidence: The cycles from claim 0 form a rank-at-most-eight hypergraph enumerable in O(n^8). Branching on every vertex of an uncovered hyperedge has depth at most k and O(8^k) nodes, giving O(8^k n^8). For approximation, the union U of a maximal vertex-disjoint short-cycle packing hits every short cycle, hence is an FVS. If the packing has p cycles, every FVS has size at least p while |U|≤8p.
claims.witness: A branch records one selected vertex from each encountered short cycle. For the approximation, maximality certifies transversality and the p disjoint cycles certify OPT≥p.
claims.search_method: Direct algorithmic and runtime analysis using claim 0; no external search.

claims.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
claims.evidence: An independent exhaustive enumeration generated every bipartite graph with the ordered Hamilton path 0-1-...-(n-1), deciding every optional opposite-parity edge and rejecting induced C4 or P8. It reproduced the counts 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0 for orders 1 through 15. Thus a graph in the subclass cannot contain a simple 15-vertex path, since the subgraph induced by such a path's vertices would occur in the enumeration. In an undirected DFS forest every edge joins ancestor-comparable vertices. The bags consisting of a vertex and its ancestors therefore form a decomposition with bag size at most 14, hence width at most 13. Standard finite connectivity-partition dynamic programming then solves FVS in polynomial time.
claims.witness: The zero count at order 15 is an independently reproduced finite certificate; the DFS ancestor bags certify width 13.
claims.search_method: Independent exhaustive generation plus a direct DFS tree-decomposition proof.

claims.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
claims.evidence: Branching on the four vertices of an uncovered C4 and using iterative deepening finds a minimum C4-transversal X in O(4^r n^{O(1)}). Claim 2 supplies a width-13 decomposition of G-X. Adding X to every bag gives width at most r+13. FVS can be solved on this decomposition by storing the deleted boundary subset and the connectivity partition of retained boundary vertices; cycle-producing edge and join operations are rejected. The number of such states, including join processing, is 2^{O(r log r)}, establishing the stated upper bound.
claims.witness: A minimum C4-transversal X and the augmented width-(r+13) decomposition are certificates for the reduction to the bounded-width FVS dynamic program.
claims.search_method: Direct branching, decomposition-width, state-count, and transition analysis.

claims.claim: Several natural routes from these reductions to the full result are blocked by explicit P8-free families: C4-transversal number is unbounded even after removing false twins; 2-connected C4-free blocks have unbounded order; and the short-cycle LP is not integral.
claims.evidence: For the half graph H_n, all open neighborhoods are distinct and the maximum C4-free induced subgraph has n+2 vertices, so its C4-transversal number is n-2. The graph consisting of m≥2 internally disjoint length-three u-v paths is bipartite, C4-free, 2-connected, and has 2m+2 vertices. Any induced path avoiding a hub has at most two vertices, one using exactly one hub has at most five, and one using both hubs cannot extend far enough without a hub chord to form P8. Finally, on K_{3,3}, the integral short-cycle transversal optimum is 2, whereas assigning 1/4 to every vertex is feasible with value 3/2.
claims.witness: The three explicit witnesses are H_n, the length-three theta graphs, and K_{3,3}.
claims.search_method: Direct symbolic verification of each family, supplemented by finite exact checks.

claims.claim: Even false-twin-free P5-free bipartite graphs have simultaneously unbounded Feedback Vertex Set optimum and unbounded treewidth: for the half graph H_n, fvs(H_n)=n-2 and tw(H_n)≥⌈n/2⌉.
claims.evidence: For the intended family range n≥2, strict neighborhood nesting makes H_n false-twin-free and 2K2-free; every induced P5 contains an induced 2K2 on its first and last edges, so H_n is P5-free. Keeping all B vertices and a_{n-1},a_n gives an induced forest of order n+2. Conversely, if at least two A vertices survive, using the two smallest indices bounds any C4-free surviving set by n+2 vertices; with at most one surviving A vertex the bound is smaller. Hence fvs(H_n)=n-2. With t=ceil(n/2), A_1,...,A_t together with B_t,...,B_n induce K_{t,n-t+1}; both sides have size at least t, and treewidth monotonicity plus tw(K_{a,b})=min(a,b) gives tw(H_n)≥t.
claims.witness: The n+2-vertex forest certifies the upper FVS bound, the C4 counting argument certifies the lower bound, and the displayed complete biclique certifies the treewidth lower bound.
claims.search_method: Direct extremal counting and complete-biclique minor/treewidth analysis, with exhaustive checks for n=2 through 7.

claims.claim: The natural induced-short-cycle covering LP has integrality gap tending to 2 already on P4-free bipartite graphs: on K_{n,n}, its integral optimum is n-1, its fractional optimum is n/2, and the ratio is 2-2/n.
claims.evidence: For n≥2, K_{n,n} is P4-free and its only induced cycles are C4s. Fewer than n-1 deletions leave at least two vertices on each side, while n-1 deletions from one side leave a forest, proving integral optimum n-1. The all-1/4 vector is feasible with value n/2. There are binom(n,2)^2 constraints and each vertex occurs in (n-1)binom(n,2) of them; summing the constraints proves every feasible fractional solution has value at least n/2. The ratio is therefore (n-1)/(n/2)=2-2/n and tends to 2.
claims.witness: The uniform 1/4 vector is a primal optimum, and the normalized sum of all C4 constraints is a matching lower-bound certificate.
claims.search_method: Exact double counting and exhaustive finite checks for n=2 through 7.

claims.claim: The factor 8 for the specific maximal-short-cycle-packing union algorithm is tight on P8-free bipartite graphs.
claims.evidence: In a disjoint union of t chordless C8 components, no component induces P8 and paths cannot cross components. The only induced short cycle in each component is its full C8, so every maximal vertex-disjoint short-cycle packing contains all t components and its union has 8t vertices. Exactly one deletion per component is necessary and sufficient, making OPT=t and the returned ratio exactly 8.
claims.witness: The family tC8 gives ratio 8 for every t≥1, independently of packing order.
claims.search_method: Direct analysis of induced subgraphs and packings, with an exact one-component check.

claims.claim: False-twin quotienting exactly preserves the P8-free bipartite setting: contracting every equal-open-neighborhood class to one representative produces a false-twin-free P8-free bipartite skeleton H with class multiplicities q_v, and every false-twin blow-up of such an H is again P8-free and bipartite.
claims.evidence: Equal-open-neighborhood classes are independent and adjacency between two classes is uniform and complete. Representatives therefore induce a bipartite P8-free graph H. If two representatives were false twins in H, their neighboring original classes—and hence their original open neighborhoods—would coincide, contradicting maximality of the quotient classes. Conversely, a blow-up preserves bipartiteness. Two clones have identical neighborhoods in every induced subgraph containing them, whereas P8 has no pair of false twins. Thus an induced P8 in a blow-up uses at most one clone per class and projects edge-and-nonedge faithfully to an induced P8 in H, a contradiction.
claims.witness: The injective projection of any hypothetical induced P8 from the blow-up to H is the contradiction certificate.
claims.search_method: Direct equivalence-class, adjacency-uniformity, and induced-subgraph projection proof.

claims.claim:
Maximum induced forests admit an exact singleton-core/pendant-bundle normal form on the false-twin quotient. If H is the quotient and q_v is the size of class v, then
α_forest(G)=max_{U⊆V(H), H[U] a forest} (|U|+α_q(H[D_U])),
where D_U={v∉U:q_v>1 and |N_H(v)∩U|≤1} and α_q denotes maximum q-weight independent-set value.
claims.evidence: If a retained class contains at least two twins and has two retained neighbors, those four vertices induce C4 because the two neighbors lie on one bipartition side. Hence such a class has at most one retained neighbor. If its retained count lies strictly between 1 and q_v, every omitted twin can be added as a leaf or isolate, contradicting maximum cardinality. Thus counts are 0, 1, or q_v. Singleton classes form U with H[U] a forest. Full nonsingleton classes form an independent set L, and each has at most one neighbor in U, so L⊆D_U. Conversely, any forest core U and independent L⊆D_U expand to H[U] with only leaves and isolates attached, hence to an induced forest of size |U|+sum_{v∈L}q_v. Maximizing L and then U proves the formula.
claims.witness: The mutually inverse constructions between maximum retained forests and pairs (U,L), with L an independent subset of D_U, certify equality in both directions.
claims.search_method: Direct canonicalization and converse-construction proof, supplemented by exhaustive comparison on 296 small bipartite blow-ups.

claims.claim: The target is polynomial-time equivalent, with multiplicities measured in unary by Q=Σ_v q_v, to optimizing the quotient formula over false-twin-free P8-free bipartite skeletons; for every fixed singleton core U, the optimal pendant-bundle completion is computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: From G, equal-neighborhood classes, H, and q are computable in polynomial time and Q=|V(G)|; claim 9 converts an optimum formula solution to an optimum induced forest and hence an FVS. Conversely, explicitly blowing up a promised skeleton has Q vertices and remains in the target class by claim 8, so a target algorithm yields the quotient optimum. Both reductions are polynomial in unary size Q. For fixed U, H[D_U] is bipartite. Maximum q-weight independent set equals total q-weight minus minimum q-weight vertex cover, and the latter is obtained by a standard s-t cut with a capacity larger than the total weight on every graph-edge arc. The remaining optimization over U is not solved by this observation.
claims.witness: The quotient/blow-up maps give the two polynomial reductions; the weighted vertex-cover min-cut gives the fixed-U completion.
claims.search_method: Direct reduction-size, reconstruction, and min-cut analysis.

target_evidence: The exact source target is an unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm for Feedback Vertex Set on P8-free bipartite graphs. The draft proves an FPT algorithm parameterized by solution size, an 8-approximation, polynomial solvability for the C4-free subclass, FPT parameterization by C4-transversal number, obstruction families, and an exact quotient normal form. None bounds k or the C4-transversal number polynomially, extends the width bound to all target graphs, or optimizes the singleton-core choice U in polynomial time. The writeup expressly identifies this gap and claims only PARTIAL resolution, so it supplies correct material progress without claiming the missing full algorithm.
